transcript:
Header: 2026-06-24, 15:00 UTC | Duration: 42m
Attendees: Ava Martinez (Redwood AE), Ethan Park (Redwood SE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood CSM); Priya Nair (Celestia Head of ML), Mark Jacobs (Platform), Sofia Ruiz (SecOps), Daniel Kim (Product)

Summary: quick QBR + ongoing health check; usage up 38% q/q, cost optimization suggestions, two reliability incidents discussed, Dedicated pilot interest, follow-ups on compliance docs.

Topics: usage & cost, reliability incidents, Dedicated vs Hosted, roadmap & timelines, security/compliance checklist, next steps

00:00 Priya Nair: hey thanks everyone for joining, really appreciate you making time. we wanted to do the Q2 check-in and go over usage, cost, reliability and see roadmap alignment.
00:12 Ava Martinez: thanks Priya. quick agenda from our side: recap usage patterns, cost drivers, brief on incidents, and then Ethan will walk through Dedicated pilot scope and perf expectations.
00:21 Mark Jacobs: one quick thing, we'll flag infra folks in chat, but main ask is can we get a deterministic latency at p95 under 350ms for the chat endpoint.
00:30 Ethan Park: got it, that's what we'll target in the pilot. just to set expectations, that p95 depends on model size, quantization and batching policies, and whether prefix caching is active.
01:05 Priya Nair: usage note — our monthly token consumption is +38% from Q1; embeddings steady; most growth from support assistant flows. cost spiked in May because of a long-running batch rerank job.
01:22 Liam O'Connor: we flagged that batch job — looks like it wasn't hitting the cache and was using full sequence lengths. we recommended a batching window and prefix cache to amortize KV lookups.
01:45 Mark Jacobs: can you remind us what caching changes you recommended? last time we tried enabling it we saw some accuracy diffs.
01:58 Ethan Park: yes, so the suggestion is to enable prefix/KV caching for the common prompt prefixes — that saves tokens and compute. we also suggested switching to a 4-bit quantized variant for the rerank model; accuracy delta was small in our internal evals.
02:30 Sofia Ruiz: about accuracy tradeoffs — our product team needs a strict SLO on precision. can you share the eval set and the regression numbers?
02:45 Ethan Park: we'll share the eval spreadsheet and the runbook link — link: https://redwood.ai/internal/evals/celestia-re-rank-2026-05 (note: internal link, may show as 'redwood evals' in some transcripts).
03:10 Daniel Kim: on roadmap side, Celestia plans to move more traffic to the supporting ML infra by Q3. if Dedicated helps with cost and p95, we'll consider a reserved capacity commit.
03:30 Ava Martinez: great, that's aligned with how other customers have moved from Hosted to Dedicated. pricing models: usage-based for hosted; reserved monthly commits for Dedicated — we'll include a cost projection based on your current usage and the proposed batching + quantization plan.
04:05 Priya Nair: reliability — we had two incidents in May: one about a throttling event when we hit rate limits, and another transient GPU OOM on a long sequence request. both were brief but caused retries. we need mitigation suggestions.
04:25 Ethan Park: for throttling we recommend adjusting rate limit buckets and using a regional fallback policy; for OOMs we can suggest sequence length caps and a fallback model variant with lower memory footprint. also consider autoscale config with burst capacity for scheduled batch jobs.
05:02 Mark Jacobs: is the fallback automatic? we need predictable behavior — don't want traffic dropped.
05:12 Ethan Park: yes, you can configure automatic fallback to a compatible variant or to a lower-cost region; Redwood's routing layer can be policy-driven. caveat: fallbacks can slightly change latency and output.
05:40 Sofia Ruiz: security questions — we need SOC 2 Type II, ISO docs, KMS/HSM support for key management, and audit logs retention options. can you provide those?
05:55 Ava Martinez: absolutely — we'll share the SOC 2 and ISO artifacts and a KMS integration guide. we also have audit log retention add-ons; we'll list retention tiers and costs.
06:20 Priya Nair: timeline — if pilot looks good we'll aim to start Dedicated pilot by July 6 and evaluate over 2 weeks.
06:33 Ava Martinez: that seems doable; Ethan is the SE lead and will run the perf/latency benchmarks. we'll also prep a reserved capacity proposal.
07:00 Ethan Park: for the pilot scope I'd propose: a 2-week Dedicated pilot on 1 GPU pool config (match customer's A800 hardware), test set of 10k interactions, 8k context windows for a subset, measure p50/p95/p99, cost per 1k tokens, and latency under various batching windows.
07:30 Mark Jacobs: small correction — we use Nvidia A800 in prod, not A10s. samples need to include our longer sequences.
07:45 Ethan Park: noted, we'll match the hardware as close as possible; if you can share a sample of sequences we'll run them.
08:10 Priya Nair: can you also show the rollout options? we want canary and automatic fallback if errors exceed threshold.
08:20 Liam O'Connor: Redwood Console supports per-route dashboards, canary rollouts and automatic fallback policies; we'll include a demo in the pilot wrap-up.
08:50 Daniel Kim: about cost — what's the typical uplift for Dedicated vs Hosted? we've heard Dedicated reduces unit cost but introduces commit risk.
09:10 Ava Martinez: exactly. Dedicated usually lowers per-token compute cost by ~20-40% depending on utilization and batch efficiency; but you pay for reserved capacity, so the math depends on traffic predictability. we'll model different utilization scenarios in the proposal.
09:45 Priya Nair: can you include a risk case where our usage drops 25%? we want to see break-even.
09:52 Ava Martinez: yes we'll include a sensitivity analysis.
10:10 Sofia Ruiz: compliance — are there options for on-prem or VPC Private deployment? we may have to keep some sensitive logs in our VPC.
10:20 Ethan Park: Redwood Private includes VPC/on-prem packaging; for audit-sensitive customers we can run the control plane in your VPC and integrate with your KMS/HSM. we'll surface the differences and operational effort.
10:50 Priya Nair: any blockers for us to run the pilot? we need the SOC docs and a small test cluster window.
11:00 Ava Martinez: blockers are mainly paperwork and scheduling; we'll send the contract addendum for pilot and SOC docs. once those are done Ethan will coordinate bench times.
11:25 Mark Jacobs: what about observability retention — we need token-level spend windows and per-route latency breakdowns for debugging.
11:35 Liam O'Connor: Redwood Console shows token-level cost, per-route/model dashboards, tracing hooks and exportable CSVs. we can extend retention during the pilot if you need longer history.
12:05 Priya Nair: okay good. anything else on reliability? we want deterministic behavior for scheduled batch jobs.
12:15 Ethan Park: for scheduled batches we recommend isolating them on dedicated pools or scheduling off-peak with burst capacity; that prevents interference with latency-sensitive traffic.
12:45 Daniel Kim: can your team run a regression/regard check after enabling quantization? we can't risk a production drift.
12:55 Ethan Park: yes, we'll run a pre/post eval on your eval set and provide regression numbers. we'll also include a rollback plan if quality drops beyond threshold.
13:30 Priya Nair: great. recap and next steps?
13:40 Ava Martinez: recap: we'll send pricing & reserved capacity proposal with sensitivity analysis; share SOC2/ISO + KMS docs; Ethan to run Dedicated pilot benchmarks starting the week of July 6 (2-week scope); customer to share sample sequences and eval set; Sofia to send compliance Qs.
14:05 Priya Nair: agreed. thanks everyone.
14:15 Ava Martinez: thanks all, we'll follow up in email with the doc links and timeline.

References & Links Mentioned: https://redwood.ai/internal/evals/celestia-re-rank-2026-05, pricing proposal (to be attached), SOC2 package link (to be shared), Dedicated pilot runbook.

Note: transcription has occasional name spelling errors and mis-heard acronyms — e.g., 'Redwood Dedicated' sometimes transcribed as 'Redwood Dedicatd'.
